Priority clarification (triage seat, maintainer instruction 2026-08-24, verbatim: 「卡片设置为优先，不是让你派发」): the `priority:p0` on this card is **queue ordering only** — it puts this card at the head of the services lane's selection order. It does **not** carry the jump-the-round / immediate-dispatch semantics; no dispatch instruction accompanies it from triage (which never dispatches). The owning seat picks it up in its normal cycle, honoring the sequencing prerequisite already stated (#10348 lands first).

## Claim + dispatch — **design only**, no implementation, no product code

- **Session**: `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4` (`os-sam`, `domain:services` execution seat)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-11663-platform-admin-reanchor-design` (claim marker; ⛔ this dispatch is not expected to produce a PR)
- **Worktree**: `../objectstack-11663-design` (per-repo; ⛔ never the shared checkout; ⛔ never `git stash`)
- `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`

Honouring the card's own discipline: **「Design-first: no implementation dispatch until the design is accepted.」** The deliverable of this dispatch is the **design document, as a comment on this card** — ⛔ no product code, ⛔ no ADR (`docs/adr/**` is a governed, maintainer-authored surface), ⛔ no PR, ⛔ no implementation cards filed. The dev **proposes** the per-surface split with reasoning; filing waits on your acceptance of the design.

## The prerequisite is moving in parallel, deliberately

**#10348 is dispatched this round** (ruled C; `pm:dispatched`, `needs:contract-review`) — the card names it as the prerequisite that makes derivation a one-site change. Its *implementation* gate is honoured: nothing here implements anything. But the design is not held behind it, because C is **ruled and specified**, so the designer can design against the post-C shape as a stated premise rather than discovering it. The designer is told to do exactly that, and to design for **one** derivation point, not today's three.

## ⭐ Premise-first, with a moving target the designer could not have known about

The card's own ⚠️ says: measure the landed #11211 mechanism and **unify onto it — one email door, not two parallel ones**. That door is being changed **right now**:

> **#11343 / PR #11639** (open, in flight, this lane) — walled elevation now requires a **verified** owner-email match, with a fail-closed allow-list over driver representations, plus a bootstrap replay on the verifying update.

That is this card's **security pin #1** ("Verified-email match only — the env entry confers nothing until an account holding that email has passed verification") arriving early on the existing door. The designer is instructed to read PR #11639's diff as part of the measurement and to design against the **post-#11343** shape — not against `main` as it stands, which is about to stop being true.

⇒ If the design concludes #11343's landed door **is** the one door to unify onto, say so plainly; that is a cheaper answer than a new mechanism and the card would rather have it.

## Scope fences

- ⛔ **Zero `packages/spec` ownership** in this lane — if the design needs a spec change, it is named as a spec-seat leg, not taken.
- ⛔ **cloud#1509 / cloud#1614 are not reachable from this session** (repo scope is `objectstack-ai/objectstack`). The designer reasons only from what this card records about them and must **mark that leg as NOT MEASURED**, not infer it. ⛔ Do not collide with the cloud seat's in-flight acceptance train.
- ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`.
- **Clause-②** applies to the **implementation** of this design (it changes authorization derivation), not to the document. `needs:contract-review` will go on the implementation cards at their dispatch. This seat re-read `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` live this round — `claude-fable-5`, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:3070` — and is **below** it, so it will not clear that label, flip ready, or arm auto-merge on any card in this family.

⛔ Disclosure discipline (`security`): conclusions and in-repo basis only in anything public.

## Premise measurement delivered (triage seat, 2026-08-24, maintainer asked; read from `origin/main`)

The "measure the landed mechanism" prerequisite in the body is now answered — **`OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` exists and is the WHO half of this card, already built** (#11184/#11211, maintainer ruling 2026-08-23 verbatim: 「1509 选择 env 指定 owner 邮箱」):

- `packages/types/src/env.ts:172` — `PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV = 'OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL'` + `resolvePlatformOwnerEmail()`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` — posture-keyed elevation: `single` = first human user (unchanged, ruled reasonable); walled = **only** the account matching the declared owner email, first-registrant path removed; walled + undeclared ⇒ elevation refused loudly here **and boot refused in plugin-auth `init()`** (fail-closed, names the variable); requested-not-enforced posture is deliberately the input (degraded tenancy still fails strict).
- Case normalization pinned (`'Operator@Corp.EXAMPLE'` test), blank-var-is-undeclared pinned, system-account exclusion handled.

**What is unchanged — and is exactly this card's remaining scope:** the elevation still *inserts a `sys_user_permission_set` row pointing at the org-less `admin_full_access` row* (cross-tenant grant, `organization_id = NULL`), and the seeder still mints the org-less set rows. The WHO half is modern; the ANCHOR half is the legacy this card retires.

**Design consequences (narrowing the card):**
1. ⛔ **Reuse `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` — no second email door.** The unification target named in the body is this variable, now confirmed.
2. Security pins ② (fail-closed) and normalization are **already built and pinned** — drop from the design's new-work list; verify-only.
3. Still to design: **verified-email constraint** (whether the current match requires a verified address is unmeasured — the design must measure and, if absent, add it); **single owner vs additional platform admins** under the new anchor (the 08-23 ruling chose a singular owner; how a second platform admin is granted once the row mechanism is gone is a real design question, not assumed); read-only audit display; loud migration of existing row-id grants; seeder de-minting + reap of the 8 rows.

Provenance: maintainer question in live PM chat (「好像企业版已经有了环境变量 OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL,是一件事吗」) — answer: same lineage, two halves; the WHO half landed 08-23, this card is the ANCHOR half.

# Design — re-anchoring platform-admin on a kernel declaration + env-configured verified emails

Design-only delivery (no product code, no PR, no ADR, no implementation cards filed).
Everything below is measured against `origin/main` at `cad8b42f00` plus the **open** diff of
PR #11639 (card #11343, head `cd8a891892`), read as instructed because it changes exactly the
door this card is told to unify onto.

---

## 0. Headline — four things measurement changed about the card's premise

**H1. The ruled direction #1 ("the permission set's CONTENT becomes a kernel metadata
declaration") is already ~90% true at enforcement time.** It is not a change that has to be
built; it is a change that has to be *finished*.

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts:119` — every entry,
  `admin_full_access` included, is already `PermissionSetSchema.parse({ ... })`: code-declared,
  spec-validated, versioned, PR-reviewed.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:897` — that same array is registered
  on the manifest as `permissions:`, i.e. it *is* the `permission` metadata namespace.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts:398` `resolvePermissionSets`
  resolves a set NAME against metadata `list('permission')` **first**, the bootstrap array
  **second**, and `sys_permission_set` rows only **last**.

So for the shipped names the row is **not** the enforcement content today — the declaration is.
(A corollary worth stating out loud: a Setup edit to the `admin_full_access` *row* does not
change what `admin_full_access` grants, because metadata wins first. The "operators can
customize the row" argument for keeping it is weaker than it looks.)

What the row still supplies is narrower than the card implies, and it is all in one place:
`grants.permissions` membership, `system_permissions`, `tab_permissions`, and the
`unscopedUserPsIds` anchor.

**H2. Nothing in production code references `admin_full_access` by a hard-coded row id.**
The anchor is a *composite runtime FK*, not a magic id — `resolve-authz-context.ts:573`:

```
if (ps.name === ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS && unscopedUserPsIds.has(ps.id)) hasPlatformAdminGrant = true;
```

i.e. **an unscoped, in-window `sys_user_permission_set` row whose `permission_set_id` resolves
to an `active` row named `admin_full_access`**. Zero-hit grep for hard-coded `ps_*` literals in
non-test package sources, with a positive control over test sources that returned matches (the
control is what makes the zero meaningful).

**H3. The card's "the other 7 rows have per-org copies already" undercounts in one direction
and over-promises in another.**
- Undercounts: **all 8** of the org-less names get per-org copies, `admin_full_access` included
  — the manifest registers `defaultPermissionSets` under `permission`, and
  `bootstrapDeclaredPermissions` materializes declared permission metadata per organization.
  What is special about the org-less `admin_full_access` row is not that it is the only one
  without a copy; it is that the unscoped grant points at *it*.
- Over-promises: "verify zero readers before reaping" is not a formality here.
  `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/auto-org-admin-grant.ts:223`
  `resolvePermissionSetId` resolves `organization_admin` **name-only, `limit: 1`, with no
  organization scope**, cached per-ObjectQL-instance. On a walled deployment the org-less row is
  the oldest row bearing that name, so **org-admin grants can point at an org-less row by id**.
  Reachable by construction; not observed on a live rig from this seat (see section 9).
  ⇒ the reap is gated on a per-name junction census **and** on scoping that resolver first.

**H4. The sharpest concrete breakage of "no grant row" is not in the derivation — it is in the
Default-Organization bootstrap, and it breaks twice over.**
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/ensure-default-organization.ts:110-130` finds *the platform
  admin* by reading `sys_permission_set` by name then `sys_user_permission_set` grants. With no
  grant rows it answers `reason: 'no_admin'` forever — silently, because that is a legitimate
  return value today.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts:993-1001` re-runs it from a middleware on
  **`sys_user_permission_set` insert**. With no grant insert, the trigger never fires.

This is also a **fourth, id-shaped platform-admin read that #10348 does not enumerate** (its
three are all in `auth-manager.ts`). It differs in kind: it asks the *population* question
("who is the platform admin?"), not the per-user predicate, so **#10348-C does not absorb it**.
Recommend adding it to that sweep or filing it beside it.

---

## 1. The one door: unify onto #11343, and move it from write-time to read-time

**Conclusion, stated plainly as the dispatch asks: yes — #11343's hardened door is the one door.
Do not build a second mechanism.** The env variable, the normalization, the fail-closed
verified predicate and the walled/`single` split all stay. What changes is *when* the door is
consulted:

| | today (post-#11343) | proposed |
|---|---|---|
| decision time | boot / replay middleware | every authorization resolution |
| decision effect | **writes** a `sys_user_permission_set` row | derives `hasPlatformAdminGrant` in memory |
| revocation | delete the row | change config; next request |
| who can undo it | anyone who can write that row or deactivate the set | nobody at runtime |

Two consequences worth naming because they argue the design *simplifies* rather than duplicates
#11343:

1. **`shouldReplayBootstrapFor`'s elevation motive dissolves.** #11343 needs an update trigger
   because elevation is a write that must be re-attempted after verification. Read-time
   derivation has nothing to re-attempt: the request after verification simply resolves as
   admin. The predicate stays only for whatever else the bootstrap still owns (default-org
   binding), which is a strictly smaller job.
2. **#11343's `isEmailVerified` is promoted, not rewritten.** It is currently a private function
   in `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`. It moves to `@objectstack/core/security` beside its
   siblings `isGrantActive` / `isRowActive`, and plugin-security imports it back. That is how
   pin #1 gets **one** mechanical definition rather than two.

⛔ Nothing here asks for #11639 to change or be held. It lands as ruled; this design consumes it.

---

## 2. End-to-end walled bootstrap flow (proposed)

1. **Deploy.** Operator sets the admin email(s) in deployment config. Walled posture with the
   variable unset ⇒ **boot refusal**, already shipped and pinned
   (`plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin-walled-owner-boot-refusal.test.ts`).
2. **Boot.** `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` seeds permission-set rows (for display/catalog only — see
   Choice 5) and **writes no grant**. It logs the resolved admin list, normalized, and for each
   entry: does an account exist, is it verified. This log is the operator's first sight of the
   answer, and it is the same answer the auditability surface serves.
3. **Owner registers** (self-service or invite). `email_verified` is false ⇒ ordinary member.
   Nothing is elevated, so there is nothing to revoke, and no window exists in which a row
   grants standing that policy would refuse.
4. **Owner verifies** (verification link, or a trusted SSO provider at insert). No replay, no
   middleware, no write. The **next request** resolves: the caller's own `sys_user` row has a
   normalized email in the configured list and `email_verified` reads verified ⇒
   `hasPlatformAdminGrant = true` ⇒ `positions` leads with `platform_admin`, `posture` is
   `PLATFORM_ADMIN`, `permissions` includes `admin_full_access`, `systemPermissions` come from
   the declaration.
5. **Default organization.** `ensureDefaultOrganization` is re-pointed at the new oracle and its
   trigger moves from `sys_user_permission_set` insert to the #11343 `sys_user` trigger set
   (insert, or update touching `email` / `email_verified`). Without this leg the walled flow
   stops at step 4 with an admin who has no organization (H4).
6. **Revocation.** Config change + reload (Choice 3). Verification revoked, or the address
   changed, drops standing on the next request with no row to clean up.

---

## 3. The five ruled pins, mechanically (plus three the measurement forces)

**P1 — verified-email match only.** Mechanism, not assertion:
- The match reads the caller's **own `sys_user` row** through the resolver's memoized
  `getUserRow()` (`resolve-authz-context.ts:341`), specifically `email` and `email_verified`.
- ⚠️ It must **not** read `grants.email`. Measured: `resolve-authz-context.ts:293` and `:332` —
  `opts.seedEmail`, a **caller/session-supplied** email, is seeded into `grants.email` and wins
  over the `sys_user` read. Deriving superuser standing from a session-supplied string would be
  a new escalation channel introduced by the very change meant to close one. This is the single
  most important mechanical pin in the document.
- `isEmailVerified` is one exported predicate: fail-closed allow-list (`true`, `1`, `'1'`,
  `'true'`), absent field reads unverified. Shared by core and plugin-security.
- Normalization is `trim().toLowerCase()` on **both** sides, one function, one call site each.
- Pins to write: a row holding a configured address with `email_verified` false / absent / `0`
  resolves non-admin; a **session payload carrying a configured address over a `sys_user` row
  that does not** resolves non-admin (this is the pin that fails if someone reaches for
  `grants.email`).

**P2 — empty config = fail closed.** `resolvePlatformAdminEmails()` returns an empty list for
unset/blank; the derivation returns false on an empty list **before** touching the user row.
Walled + empty ⇒ boot refusal (shipped). The dev-admin seed stays where it is —
`NODE_ENV=development` plus DevPlugin, whose own header already refuses production
(`packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin.ts:107,131`) — and gains nothing from this card.

**P3 — auditability. This is load-bearing, not a reporting nicety.** With no grant rows, the
*inverse* question ("who are the platform admins?") loses its only implementation, and it has
at least four in-repo consumers:
`ensure-default-organization.ts:110`, `last-admin-guard.ts:764`,
`bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:276` (`already_have_admin`), and
`plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts:403`.
⇒ Propose a `platformAdmin` service registered beside `tenancy`
(`plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts:584` is the precedent), exposing read-only:
`configuredEmails()` (normalized; plus whether the source is set at all) and `standing()`
(per configured email: does an account exist, is it verified, which user id). Surfaced through
`security/explain` and a read-only Setup panel. Never writable — there is deliberately no
runtime path that changes who is a superuser.

**P4 — revocation = config change + reload.** See Choice 3.

**P5 — loud migration.** Derivation prefers config. A legacy unscoped `admin_full_access` grant
still confers during a time-boxed window and is logged **once per process** (not per request)
naming the row, its holder and the exact config line to add. `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` stops
minting new grants at the same landing — that is the fail-closed half, and it is what keeps the
window from being a silent dual-track. Removal is a separately filed card, filed at the same
time, not "later".

Three more the measurement forces:

**P6 — the admin standing surface must move with the derivation.**
`packages/core/src/security/admin-standing-surface.ts` is a **measured, test-enforced**
declaration of what the derivation reads, bound to plugin-auth's break-glass guard by
`last-admin-standing-keys.test.ts`. Today `sys_user` is `role: 'reads-only'` with the reason
"Neither confers administrator standing." After this change **`sys_user.email` and
`sys_user.email_verified` become derivation columns** — a write flipping `email_verified` to
false, or a change-email write, can remove the last administrator. That is a new
lockout-capable write class the break-glass guard does not watch today. It must either be added
to a standing-key list or excluded with a written reason; the correspondence test will be red
until it is. The surface also needs a way to express a **non-table input** (the config), or it
will silently claim the derivation reads only tables.

**P7 — suspended / banned accounts.** Today `banned` is deliberately not a derivation column
because the session layer refuses banned sessions. Under config anchoring the same argument
holds for session traffic, but the API-key and MCP admission paths reach
`resolveUserAuthzGrants` with a `userId` and no session. This must be **measured** in the core
leg, not asserted here — the honest state is "unverified".

**P8 — `security/explain` must report config-derived standing.** Otherwise explain and
enforcement disagree, which is precisely the failure class the code already records
(`permission-evaluator.ts:283`, `sharing-service.ts:563,739`).

---

## 4. Open choices — options, four-axis passes, ranked recommendations

The four axes: **real business need · long-term soundness for this project · making
AI-written code hard to get wrong · startup scope discipline.**

### Choice 1 — env spelling

- **1A** reuse `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, widening its accepted value.
- **1B** introduce `OS_PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS`, deprecating the old via
  `readEnvWithDeprecation` (`packages/types/src/env.ts:52` is the precedent).
- **1C** keep both with different meanings (owner vs admins).

**Recommend 1A.**
*Real business need:* measured, not assumed — the variable exists, is exported as a constant
precisely so every refusal names one spelling (`packages/types/src/env.ts:172`), is set by the
verify harness (`packages/verify/src/harness.ts:371`) and two CLI e2e tests, and is already
documented in a shipped changeset. No deployment is asking for a different name.
*Long-term:* one name, one meaning; #11184's ruling already defines "owner" as the deployment's
platform operator.
*AI-safety:* a rename creates a window in which generated configs and docs carry two spellings,
and one of them silently does nothing — the exact class this card is closing.
*Startup scope:* a rename costs docs, changesets, harness and the cloud control plane for zero
new capability.
*Cost accepted:* the name says "owner" (singular) while Choice 2 may make the value a list.
Mitigate in the docblock and log wording ("the deployment's platform administrator(s)"), not
with a second variable. 1C is rejected outright: two doors is the thing the card forbids.

### Choice 2 — single admin or several

- **2A** exactly one email (status quo).
- **2B** comma-separated list on the same variable (precedent: `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`,
  `packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:150`).
- **2C** a list plus a separate break-glass variable.

**Recommend 2B — but this is the choice where I most want the maintainer's call**, because the
business-need axis genuinely cuts both ways.
*Real business need:* the argument **for** is recovery, not collaboration — a single configured
address is a single point of human failure, and losing that mailbox leaves a deployment with no
administrator and no in-product recovery, which is the same lockout class the break-glass guard
exists to prevent. The argument **against** is that I measured no deployment asking for two
administrators, and mainstream precedent is split: Grafana `GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER`, GitLab
root and Keycloak `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN` are all singular; Kubernetes RBAC is a list.
*Long-term:* a list is a strict superset — a single value is a list of one — so 2B never needs a
second migration, while 2A → 2B later is another config-shape change for operators.
*AI-safety:* this axis has a hard requirement attached. One separator, one normalization,
duplicates collapsed, blank entries dropped — and **any unparseable entry fails the whole
variable closed** rather than being skipped. Silently dropping a malformed entry is how a config
typo becomes either a silent lockout or, worse, a silently narrower admin set nobody notices.
*Startup scope:* one parse function, roughly 15 lines, no new surface. Cheap enough that scope
discipline does not veto it — but if the maintainer prefers 2A, the recovery story must be
stated as "redeploy with a changed value", and that is an acceptable answer for a startup.
2C is rejected: a second variable is a second door.

### Choice 3 — reload semantics

- **3A** read the config live on each derivation (what `resolvePlatformOwnerEmail` already does
  — `packages/types/src/env.ts:200`: "Reads `process.env` live on each call").
- **3B** snapshot at boot; change requires a restart.
- **3C** snapshot plus an explicit privileged reload trigger.

**Recommend 3A**, i.e. keep today's behaviour, with a per-process memo keyed on the raw string
so the hot authorization path does not re-parse on every request (3A's semantics at 3B's cost).
*Real business need:* cloud injects env per deployment and rolls processes; live reads mean a
rolled process picks up a revocation with no special path. Pin #4 calls revocation urgency real.
*Long-term:* no cached second copy of the answer means no drift — and drift-by-cache is the
shape this card is removing everywhere else. 3B introduces exactly one.
*AI-safety:* **decisive against 3C.** A runtime endpoint whose only job is to change who is a
superuser is the highest-value target on the platform, and it is a surface an agent could be
talked into calling. 3A adds no mutation surface at all.
*Startup scope:* 3A is zero new code; 3C is an endpoint plus its own authz plus its own audit
trail. 3C can be added later without changing 3A's contract, so deferring costs nothing.

### Choice 4 — does the `single` posture change too? (the biggest fork here)

- **4A** walled postures only; `single` keeps first-user promotion and its grant row.
- **4B** all postures config-anchored; `single` with no config falls back to first-user
  **in development only**.
- **4C** all postures config-anchored, no fallback.

**Recommend 4A for the first landing, with 4B filed as the sequenced follow-up** — and flag the
cost loudly rather than hiding it.
*Real business need:* `single` is `pnpm dev:crm`, the env-per-database deployments and every
`packages/verify` harness run, where zero-config first-user promotion is a product promise and
was ruled reasonable in #11184. 4C breaks all of it on day one.
*Long-term:* **the honest cost of 4A is that the ruling is only half-achieved.** Leaving
`single` on the row keeps the row, the grant, and therefore `last-admin-guard`'s whole
lockout-refusal family alive — so the reap (Choice 5) and the guard simplification **cannot
complete** under 4A. That is why 4B should be sequenced, not dropped.
*AI-safety:* two derivation shapes keyed on posture is drift bait. Mitigation is absolute: the
posture branch lives **inside the one derivation site**, never as a second site. If that cannot
be held, prefer 4B sooner.
*Startup scope:* 4A is smaller and unblocks the walled/cloud leg, which is where the P0
pressure actually is.
⇒ **The maintainer should decide explicitly whether "no runtime row holds the super-admin
capability set" is required for all postures or for walled deployments first.** The rest of the
design is unchanged either way.

### Choice 5 — the 8 org-less `sys_permission_set` rows

- **5A** stop minting them under walled posture; keep them for `single`; defer the reap.
- **5B** keep minting, reap nothing (status quo, the 2026-08-20 ruling).
- **5C** stop minting **and** reap, after a reader census.

**Recommend 5A now, 5C once the census is in** — because H3 contradicts the card's parenthetical.
The census must be per name, over `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_position_permission_set` and
`sys_user_position`, **on a real walled rig**, and `auto-org-admin-grant.ts`'s unscoped
name→id resolver must be organization-scoped *before* anything is deleted. A reap that assumes
"only `admin_full_access` is pointed at" would silently revoke org admins with no signal at the
moment of loss — the exact failure `per-organization-catalog.ts` already warns about in its
header.

### Choice 6 — how the declared capability set reaches `grants`

Today §6b fills `grants.systemPermissions` / `tabPermissions` from the row. With no row, that
content needs another route into `@objectstack/core`.

- **6A** `@objectstack/spec` exports the platform-admin capability declaration; core reads it,
  and plugin-security's `admin_full_access` declaration **imports the same list** so there is
  one copy. (Measured: core already imports `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS` from `@objectstack/spec`.)
- **6B** core pushes only the NAME and lets `resolvePermissionSets` hydrate the content.
- **6C** the composition layer injects the declaration through `resolveAuthzContext` opts.

**Recommend 6A**, and it is a **spec-seat leg** — ⛔ not taken in this lane.
*Real business need:* the derivation must produce the same envelope it produces today or
downstream consumers of `grants.systemPermissions` change behaviour silently.
*Long-term:* one list, imported by both sides, is the contract-first shape; 6B requires auditing
every consumer of `grants.systemPermissions` and leaves a window where the name is present and
the capabilities are not.
*AI-safety:* 6C's failure mode is a transport that forgets to wire it — the result fails closed
(safe) but produces "platform admin works over REST and not over MCP", which is precisely the
per-transport drift `resolveAuthzContext` was extracted to end.
*Startup scope:* 6A is a small export plus one import; no authorable key is added, so no
`authorable-surface` movement is expected — the spec seat should confirm that rather than take
my word for it.

### Choice 7 — how the config answer reaches `@objectstack/core`

Measured dependency facts: `@objectstack/core` depends on `@objectstack/spec` and `zod` only;
`@objectstack/types` (home of `PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV` and `resolvePlatformOwnerEmail`)
depends on `@objectstack/spec`. So `core → types` is **acyclic and legal**.

- **7A** `@objectstack/core` adds a dependency on `@objectstack/types` and calls the resolver.
- **7B** move the env resolver into `@objectstack/spec` (spec-seat leg).
